description:
STEP 2 (re-key on the arrow). Code-review finding 2. Captures (capture_tys ++ surface.inputs) are NOT part of the source arrow; ~50 sites slice .input positionally (capture/param split at runtime_demand.rs:1428-1434, callable_flow_resolutions builds inputs = capture_tys ++ surface.inputs at 1905-1941).

Model captures as LEADING addressed slots: a closure activation surface is (cap0..capK, param0..) -> r0, minted where the closure forms; the source contract arrow is the param SUFFIX. Replace every positional .input[i] / .input[..k] / .input[k..] consumer (~50, including the capture/param split) with structural projection BY ADDRESS (slot 1 <-> slot 1, no positional zip; addresses align the slots).

Re-verify the ~50 count and exact sites against HEAD before starting (runtime_demand.rs has moved since proposal authoring).

Depends on: re-key ActivationKey (fz-hwn.27.6).
Checks: closure/capture fixtures (Enum.reduce, nested direct-callable captures) stay green; capture/param split reads by address; no raw positional slice of .input survives. Lib + matrix green, zero warnings.

comments.text: Co-landing: not separable from 27.6 (proven empirically). Activation key inputs = capture_tys ++ surface.inputs, so the capture-slot model and the input re-key are the same change -- abi_ready_matches_direct_callable_captures_by_canonical_activation_key fails the moment inputs are re-keyed without it. See 27.6 finding.

fz-hwn.27.5 probe finding — RETARGET this ticket at the real root cause.

The phantom's activation KEY is correctly addressed (proved: re-addressing key.inputs is a no-op, changed=false). The divergence is in VALUE_TYPES, not the key. Same logical first param of FunctionId(164):
  - key input:  address a0  (addressed path, canonical)
  - value_type: α0          (alpha_normalize_vars via world.rs:716, the OLD path)
One logical variable, TWO canonical frames. This is almost certainly why phantom_resolution_keys cannot match the value-template against a ground sibling to prune it (frames don't line up), so the phantom reaches the backend.

Scope: address an activation's value_types (at least param/capture-bound ones) in the SAME scope as its key — params/captures as addressed slots — and DELETE the frame-divergent alpha_normalize_vars survivors: world.rs:716 (define_activation_analysis value_types), :848 (define_activation_return evidence), :892/:894 (callsite summary return_ty). These are NOT benign standalone canonicalization; they produce a frame that diverges from the addressed key. This is the cure for fz-hwn.23; the .27.5 predicate is the flag, not the cure.

Retarget comment (2026-06-20T16:13:20Z) is SUPERSEDED. Its premise — value_types frame divergence is 'the cure for fz-hwn.23' — was disproven: fz-hwn.23 is fixed (c1f1b55fb) by cross-activation surface grounding, and the gate reads addressed ActivationKey.inputs, never value_types (removing the alpha_normalize_vars on value_types changed nothing). This ticket reverts to its ORIGINAL scope: captures as leading addressed slots, replacing positional .input slicing with structural projection by address. NOTE: the fz-hwn.23 fix already does the capture/surface split PRAGMATICALLY (ground_surface_for_template slices inputs[captures_len..], captures threaded unchanged) — 27.8 is the principled structural home for that split.

title: Captures as leading addressed slots: replace positional .input slicing with structural projection
